text:
taylor: FYI saw repeated p99 blips when host staging kicks off. looks like our demote decision is too all-or-nothing, and small concurrent batches get hammered during the compaction wave.

mira: can you summarize the observable chain? where does the latency actually spike?

taylor: pattern: stage trigger -> immediate bulk demotes -> eviction queue spikes -> lots of small compactions -> token-level latency p99 up for ~3-6s -> downstream fallbacks (smaller model) cause kvcache churn. spike spans both drain and short warmup.

jonah: sounds like we need a graded demote instead of emergency-on. suggest two ideas: (A) demote-rate as a continuous knob (0..1) derived from an "evict_pressure" scalar, (B) soft-demote credits so tenants can be given limited elective demotes per-window. both tenant-aware.

devin: i'm leaning to rate + credits. credits prevent a runaway tenant from doing repeated elective demotes during a hot window. rate smoothing prevents the spike when multiple tenants demote concurrently.

mira: what does the math look like?

jonah: prototyped this metric: evict_pressure = smooth(queue_len, 1s) * (1 + rel_drop(resident_score)) where rel_drop = max(0, (prev - curr)/prev). then demote_rate = sigmoid((evict_pressure - thresh) / scale) * max_demote_rate.

```
# example params
thresh=6.0
scale=3.0
max_demote_rate=10 # demotes/sec across host
```

# soft credits
credits_window_s=60
credits_per_window=4

# per-tenant weighting: tenant_share = tenant_quota / sum(active_quotas)
```

mira: good. a few concerns: 1) if free memory collapses, we must bypass smoothing and force demotes. 2) compaction scheduling needs to be aware of demote_rate so we don't launch too many tiny compactions concurrently. 3) telemetry.

taylor: agreed. safety rules: if free_pages_pct < 4% -> emergency_demote(). otherwise apply rate. compaction adaptor: take demote_rate and cap concurrent_compactions = min(ceil(demote_rate), compaction_global_cap). also add compaction_batching window (50-150ms) to coalesce small demotes.

devin: operationally, add a per-host penalty token for routing. if host keeps demote_rate low, router can de-prioritize until it stabilizes. simpler than global coordinator for now.

jonah: telemetry candidates: "evict_pressure", "demote_rate", "credits_used_by_tenant", "compactions_inflight", "p99_while_demote_rate>0". Also log the decision reason for each demote attempt.

mira: test plan: unit tests for boundary cases of sigmoid mapping, integration test with synthetic workload that triggers staging and asserts p99 reduction, and a 48h canary on QA with credits enabled. metrics to check: p50/p95/p99, OOMs, cross-host request skew.

devin: rollouts: 1) feature flag off by default; 2) enable in QA cluster (all hosts); 3) enable in prod small shard (5 hosts); 4) expand if stable. include an emergency bailout toggle.

jonah: quick failure-mode notes: - if credits mis-configured, low-priority tenants could be blocked; ensure tenant_quota defaults to fair-share. - if sigmoid scale too small, small fluctuations cause big rate changes; default scale=3 seems stable in local tests.

mira: add observability: emit histogram of evict_pressure per-tenant and a counter for emergency_demotes. add an alert: emergency_demotes > 3 in 5m.

taylor: sample logs from local sim:
```
[13:12:02] evict_pressure=12.4 demote_rate=7.3 credits_left=2 tenant=search-svc comp_inflight=3
[13:12:04] demote_attempt tenant=search-svc allowed=true reason=proportional_rate
[13:12:05] compaction_start comp_id=42 size=128kb
```

mem-bot: alert: host-7 free_pages_pct=3.8% emergency_demote triggered, p95=520ms

mira: saw mem-bot. good that we have emergency bypass. next steps: taylor open PR with config knobs, metrics, unit tests for mapping function, and a short runbook for SRE. i'll review the tests.

taylor: will do. tagging @jonah for compaction adaptor review and @devin for routing penalty integration. thanks.
